\section[a faculdade]{a faculdade — the faculty (of a university); the ability}

\label{lesson:PT-C376-faculdade}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the list of marks, then the Portuguese for the school subject.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a faculdade}
\textbf{a faculdade} — \textquotedblleft{}the faculty (of a university); the ability\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ele estuda na faculdade de medicina.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He studies at the faculty of medicine.}
\end{quote}

In Portugal people often say \emph{a faculdade} for university.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{faculdade} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{facultās} \textquotedblleft{}capability, power, means\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{facul}, \emph{facilis} \textquotedblleft{}easy, doable\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the list of marks, then the Portuguese for the school subject, then say \emph{a faculdade} again

\section[o caloiro]{o caloiro — the first-year student, the fresher}

\label{lesson:PT-C376-caloiro}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the school subject, then the Portuguese for the faculty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o caloiro}
\textbf{o caloiro} — \textquotedblleft{}the first-year student, the fresher\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Os caloiros chegam em setembro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The first-year students arrive in September.}
\end{quote}

European Portuguese; in Brazil \emph{o calouro}. Feminine \emph{a caloira}.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \emph{caloiro} is not settled; it is often linked with Greek \emph{kalógēros} \textquotedblleft{}good old man, monk\textquotedblright{}, through an old word for a novice monk. EtymDB has no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a inscrição]{a inscrição — the enrolment, the registration; the inscription}

\label{lesson:PT-C376-inscricao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the faculty, then the Portuguese for the first-year student.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a inscrição}
\textbf{a inscrição} — \textquotedblleft{}the enrolment, the registration; the inscription\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A inscrição no curso custa cinquenta euros.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Enrolment on this course costs fifty euros.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Fazer a inscrição} — to enrol, to sign up.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{inscrição} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{īnscrīptiō} \textquotedblleft{}a writing upon, an inscription, a title\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), from \emph{īnscrībere}, on \emph{scrībere} \textquotedblleft{}to write\textquotedblright{}: your name written on the list.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[o semestre]{o semestre — the semester, the half-year}

\label{lesson:PT-C376-semestre}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the first-year student, then the Portuguese for the enrolment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o semestre}
\textbf{o semestre} — \textquotedblleft{}the semester, the half-year\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Este semestre tenho cinco cadeiras.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{This semester I have five course units.}
\end{quote}

In Portuguese universities a course unit is \emph{uma cadeira}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{semestre} comes from Latin \emph{sēmestris} \textquotedblleft{}of six months, half-yearly\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{sex} \textquotedblleft{}six\textquotedblright{} and \emph{mēnsis} \textquotedblleft{}month\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a propina]{a propina — the tuition fee}

\label{lesson:PT-C376-propina}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the enrolment, then the Portuguese for the semester.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a propina}
\textbf{a propina} — \textquotedblleft{}the tuition fee\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
As propinas da faculdade subiram.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The university fees have gone up.}
\end{quote}

European Portuguese for university fees; in Brazil \emph{a propina} is a bribe, and the fee is \emph{a mensalidade}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{propina} comes from Late Latin \emph{propīna} (EtymDB), built on Latin \emph{propīnāre} \textquotedblleft{}to drink to someone's health, to hand over\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short): first a tip, then a fee.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a propina}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the enrolment, then the Portuguese for the semester, then say \emph{a propina} again
